newsitem.title: USA: Barney's co-chairmen told to pay Isetan $167 mln.
newsitem.headline: Barney's co-chairmen told to pay Isetan $167 mln.

text.p: A Manhattan Supreme Court judge on Tuesday ordered the co-chairman of upscale men's clothing retailer Barney's Inc to pay the roughly $167 million they personally guaranteed on a loan from their former Japanese business partner, Isetan Co Ltd.

The ruling, brought down by Judge Herman Cahn, is the result of a summary judgement motion Isetan filed in January 1996, two days after Barney's filed for protection under Chapter 11 bankruptcy. Cahn had enough information to rule in Isetan's favor without hearing the case in court.

Isetan sought to recover 11 loans to co-chairmen Eugene and Robert Pressman totaling $180 million it made between December 1993 and July 1994. The loans were part of more than $600 million Isetan has invested in Barney's since 1989 and is trying to recover through lawsuits on such matters as Isetan's use of Barney's name and trademark in Japan and whether or not Isetan is a Barney's landlord or equity partner.

"It's just one of the issues that has to be resolved between Isetan and Barney's," said someone close to Barney's, who stressed that Tuesday's ruling involves the Pressmans alone and that Barney's had no comment.
The person said the Pressmans -- who would have to pay over $200 million with interest on the loans and legal fees taken into consideration -- will appeal.
Isetan, for its part, was "delighted" with the decision, a lawyer representing the company said.

"Isetan is delighted and especially gratified that the judge was able to see through the Pressman's smokescreen," said Robert Brundige, a partner at the New York-based law firm Hughes, Hubbard & Reed. "Isetan is now entitled to seek to enforce the judgement against the Pressmans and realize as much as possible on that judgement."

But analysts said that, despite Tuesday's ruling, the battle between Barney's and Isetan is far from over. Last week, for example, a bankruptcy judge denied a summary judgement motion by Barney's, which claimed Isetan's leases on Barney's three flagship stores are not "true leases."
"I think this thing is just going to continue to roll for a while," said Stacy Pak, an analyst at CS First Boston, adding: "We're probably going to see some bids for Barney's."

Dickson Concepts has already said it would pay about $350 million for Barney's and there has been speculation that both Saks Holdings Inc's Saks Fifth Avenue and Neiman Marcus Group Inc are interested in making a run for the upscale retailer.
One analyst, who asked her name not be used, said Barney's is likely to sell for at least $350 million.
